input.question: Your organization uses shared admin accounts with session logging for CII SCADA systems because the legacy HMIs don't support individual authentication. The CISO argues this satisfies CCoP access control requirements through compensating controls. Does this approach comply with CCoP 2.0?

ground_truth.expected_response: Shared admin accounts on CII SCADA systems do not comply with CCoP 2.0 access control requirements, even with session logging as a compensating control. While Clause 5.2.1(c) permits shared user accounts where they are necessary for operating the CII, privileged access to CII separately requires multi-factor authentication under Clause 5.3.1(c) — and shared admin credentials on legacy HMIs cannot satisfy this MFA obligation. Session logging is a detective control that records activity after the fact; it cannot meet the preventive MFA requirement of 5.3.1(c), and the CIIO must also maintain per-account activity monitoring under Clause 5.2.1(d). The CISO cannot unilaterally treat compensating controls as equivalent to the mandated MFA. The appropriate path is to request a waiver from the specific provisions under Section 11(7) of the Cybersecurity Act 2018 (per CCoP Clause 1.6.2), submitting a written request to the Commissioner with justifications documenting the technical constraints and the proposed compensating controls.

key_facts.fact: Clause 5.3.1(c) mandates multi-factor authentication for privileged access to the CII; shared admin credentials on legacy HMIs cannot satisfy this.
Clause 5.2.1(c) permits shared user accounts only where necessary for operating the CII — it does not waive the separate MFA obligation for privileged access.
Clause 5.2.1(d) requires mechanisms to monitor the activities of each account for anomalies; session logging is a detective control that cannot substitute for the preventive MFA requirement.
A CIIO may request a waiver from specific provisions under Section 11(7) of the Cybersecurity Act 2018 by written request to the Commissioner with justifications (CCoP Clause 1.6.2).
